observations.title: Generated archive guide still includes subpath in its origin-isolation claim
observations.analysis: operatorGuide emits an OPERATOR.md statement that includes subpath alongside clearnet/onion/I2P in a sentence asserting separate browser storage, sessions and wallet permissions. A subpath alone does not create a distinct origin. The actual CLI and Tor recipe correctly retain dedicated-origin checks and warnings, so this is a surviving documentation inconsistency, not a demonstrated isolation bypass. OPERATOR.md is archive metadata, not part of the exported website.
observations.impact_limit: May mislead an operator reading the archive guide in isolation; no changed browser origin policy, key disclosure, authorization bypass or tested runtime impact is established.
observations.remediation: Describe storage and permission separation in terms of distinct origins (scheme, hostname and port). State explicitly that paths on the same origin share origin storage, and align OPERATOR.md with the current CLI and Tor runbook.

review_conclusions.conclusion: The new Tor recipe requires a primitive lowercase expected archive SHA-256, checks for its matching _headers policy, and rechecks the hash on the private copy used for generation. ZIP entry/path checks and extracted-tree verification precede export. Static exports omit hidden/never-served paths and use a fresh output tree.

The feature centralizes checksum-valid, canonical HTTP onion-origin validation, rejects unsupported ports/normalization, and aligns advertised origins with virtual port 80. Export/preview/nginx all apply the shared header policy; generated transport headers are clearnet-only. The application intentionally retains https:/wss: connect sources for explicit application endpoints.

Using all three documented Compose files removes published ports and the web publishing network; the web service remains on site_internal while Tor receives separate egress. The Tor build context allowlists only build/startup inputs. The identity volume is mounted only by Tor, with non-root/read-only/capability restrictions and startup ownership/mode checks.

review_conclusions.area: Workflow secret boundary and build handoff
review_conclusions.conclusion: The workflow is validation-only, uses a pull_request trigger rather than a privileged pull_request_target flow, declares contents:read, disables persisted checkout credentials, and supplies no deployment/signing secret to the reviewed steps. It builds the lean static workspace before packaging and tests the resulting archive. The locally computed CI checksum binds test bytes but does not establish publisher authentication.

The shared static-export change preserves source mtimeMs as string seconds, including pre-epoch values. The assigned regression sources cover fractional-second, epoch and pre-epoch cases; no test execution or runtime result is claimed.

qualification_limits.description: No repository test, build, install, server, Docker command, Tor bootstrap, network probe or browser acceptance was executed. The browser-acceptance script explicitly uses ordinary loopback Chromium, blocks external HTTP(S)/WebSocket traffic, and does not establish Tor Browser or external-wallet routing.

The source enforces the configured Tor archive hash before extraction and the configured runtime floor/PoW/GPL checks. This review did not independently retrieve or verify upstream source/checksum/signature material or validate container image digests. The runbook itself records that upstream signature verification is still pending and that distro packages vary at build time.

The port/network isolation conclusion depends on applying the final compose.onion.yaml override in the documented order. Routine updates must preserve the Compose project identity volume. These requirements are explicit in the generated guide and recipe documentation; the audit did not activate any deployment.
